source.hypothesis: Manual p188 says a START-dependent mission immediately aborts during call or assignment if any precedent lands without reaching the fixed mission success point with MNOS; otherwise it may assign systems but cannot launch until precedents complete.

model.precedent: RECON fixed at hour 8, duration 4, one aircraft, MSUCPT 1.0 and MNOS 1
model.dependent: FOLLOW fixed at hour 10, duration 2, one aircraft, allocation may begin at 9
model.dependency: one explicit FOLLOW START depends on RECON at hour 8; paired control omits only this row and changes label
model.failure: System.FRT 0 to 300000 per million OPHOURS, one half-hour direct system repair at BASE-01, seed 1; RECON MSUCPT 0.25 to 1.0 so a pre-return failure cannot accidentally follow its success point; FOLLOW MissionType.MFF 1e-6 to suppress a later independent FOLLOW failure. Both inputs share all settings.

predeclared_native_gate: Both frozen inputs derive exactly from the accepted A13 dependency model; the only control-versus-dependency semantic delta is the one MissionDependence START row. All 14 control and 15 dependency populated source business tables import and export exactly.

The guarded session-0 SSH runner preserves GUI PID 13340 and Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue, verifies source/executable fingerprints before and after, and seals all raw artifacts without overwriting prior runs.
Both models must convert with zero errors and produce a valid SXO, event log and complete 48-bin System and Stock reports. A zero calc exit code alone is insufficient.

The seed must cause RECON's assigned aircraft to have a critical system failure before its full-completion success point and return; the failed predecessor must land without a native mission success event. Failure identity and timing must match between the control and dependency runs. If these conditions fail, this candidate is diagnostic NO-GO.
The no-row control must allow FOLLOW to launch and complete without its own critical failure; otherwise the dependency effect is not isolated and the candidate is NO-GO.

The START-row run must show whether FOLLOW can assign before RECON's failed return and then abort/cancel rather than launch after a failed precedent. Accept only what individual native events and reconciled 48-bin aircraft, failure, repair and stock ledgers prove; a contradictory or ambiguous timeline is NO-GO.
A separate read-only reviewer independently replays frozen source, raw closure, native events and report ledgers without importing the author validator.
limits: One fixed seed and one failure mechanism; stochastic failure time is observed, not predicted by the seed or assumed to generalize.
This probe covers a failed predecessor. An unfinished, absent or multiple predecessor, cross-unit identity, GUI visual content and cross-engine behavior remain unverified.

excluded_diagnostics.reason: The inherited RECON MSUCPT=0.25 could place the seeded failure after the internal success point. Independent pre-run review rejected it; v1.0.0 was not run natively or published.

Native control conversion, calculation and report succeeded and showed RECON failure at 9.8829 plus FOLLOW success at 12, but the roundtrip checker incorrectly expected 13 populated control tables rather than 14 after SystemRepair was added. Runner exit was nonzero; this run remains a sealed diagnostic. v1.0.2 corrects checker counts without changing either input source.
